title: Redwood discovery - model selection with Peregrine Systems
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment
summary: Intro discovery call to surface model selection criteria for Peregrine's customer service and search augmentation use cases. Discussed context window needs (40k+ tokens for long conversations), multilingual support for EN/ES/FR, tool-calling for internal APIs, and the tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Agreed to run a POC benchmark on Redwood Dedicated with two model variants and to share pricing and security docs.
next_steps: Jesse to send pricing deck and Dedicated capacity options (by 2026-12-27)
Maya to coordinate POC benchmark (setup + test plan) and share instructions (by 2026-12-29)
Customer to provide sample convo dataset and target evaluation metrics (by 2027-01-03)
Schedule technical POC kickoff (30-45 min) week of 2027-01-04
action_items: Jesse Carter: Share pricing + Dedicated capacity examples; due 2026-12-27
Maya Lin: Draft POC test plan and infra checklist (what we need from Peregrine); due 2026-12-29
Liam O'Neil (Customer): Upload sample conversations and current embedding index snapshot; due 2027-01-03
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jesse Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Lin (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (CTO, Peregrine), Liam O'Neil (ML Eng, Peregrine), Sofia Ruiz (PM)

00:00 Jesse: Hi everyone, thanks for making time this afternoon, happy holidays - quick intros, I'm Jesse Carter from Redwood, AE on the account...
00:12 Aisha: Hi, thanks. I'm Aisha, CTO at Peregrine Systems, we run customer support automation and a semantic search layer on top of docs.
00:20 Liam: Liam here, we'll be the hands-on ML guy for the POC.
00:25 Sofia: Sofia, product, focusing on user flows for long conversations.
00:33 Jesse: Great. The goal for today is to understand your model selection needs - context window, multilingual, tool-calling, and whether Hosted, Dedicated or Private fits. Maya will jump into technical tradeoffs.
00:45 Maya: Quick clarifying question - what workloads are highest priority? Is it chat agents, extraction, reranking, embed searches?
00:58 Aisha: Primary is chat agent for customer support - long threads that reference manuals, plus a reranking layer for search. We also need Spanish and French in addition to English.
01:10 Jesse: Understood. Any constraints on latency or cost?
01:15 Aisha: Latency needs to be sub-1s for short queries but acceptable to have 2-3s for long context. Cost is material - we have a monthly budget for inference that needs to scale.
01:28 Liam: Also security - we need SOC2, SSO, and key management. We might need VPC or even an on-prem option for certain customers.
01:38 Maya: Cool. On model selection, couple axes: context length, model family and size, quantization compatibility (for Dedicated on GPUs), and whether the model supports tool/function calling natively. For example, Llama 3 variants and Mixtral-style open models support tool-calling via standard invocation, Mistral instruction-tuned models have different tokenization behavior.
02:00 Liam: We're particularly interested in >40k token context to keep long conversation state without expensive retrieval. Do you host models with that context?
02:10 Jesse: On Hosted we have curated model variants that go up to 32k and 65k in some cases depending on model. Dedicated and Private let you pin larger context builds; we can compile kernels and select memory strategies to get to 64k or more, though it depends on model architecture and GPU memory.
02:28 Maya: There's also prefix/KV caching - if many messages are repetitive or you can chunk state, we often cache the KV up to a point to reduce compute. But for very long full-sequence attention, you need models with native long-context support or a retrieval architecture.
02:45 Sofia: For multilingual, we want consistent quality across EN/ES/FR - do you have benchmarks?
02:52 Maya: We do. Our model catalog includes multilingual test sets; typically some Llama 3 multilingual mixtures and certain Mistral forks do well. But there are tradeoffs: smaller multilingual models sometimes lag in rare-language idioms. We can share our benchmark sheet.
03:10 Jesse: I'll share the catalog and our bench sheet. Note that on Dedicated you can run quantized variants which drop cost - 4-bit/8-bit - but we validate for quality regressions.
03:23 Liam: Tool-calling is important - we need models to call internal APIs to fetch order status and then synthesize replies. Any limitations?
03:32 Maya: Function-calling patterns work at the Redwood API layer; models that can emit structured JSON or follow tool schemas are straightforward. Some open weights are noisier with strict schema output; we add a small post-processing schema-checker. For strict formatting, we often recommend instruction-tuned variants or light few-shot examples.
03:52 Aisha: If we go Dedicated, will we get the same API surface as Hosted? We don't want to rework integration.
03:58 Jesse: Yes - same API, same SDKs. Dedicated is just isolated capacity with reserved GPUs and the same control plane. Private adds VPC-specific networking and optionally an on-prem package for air-gapped environments.
04:13 Sofia: Are there performance differences between Hosted and Dedicated?
04:18 Maya: Hosted can run on a variety of hardware; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput - lower jitter. Latency SLOs are easier to guarantee on Dedicated because of reserved slots and tuning. Also Dedicated lets you choose heavier models or custom kernel builds for better latency/cost.
04:36 Liam: For POC, we want to test two model families: one larger high-quality (e.g., Llama 3 70B-ish or Falcon-40B) and one optimized smaller multilingual model (Mixtral/Mistral 8x7B style) that we can quantize. Then compare cost, latency, and answer quality across EN/ES/FR.
04:59 Maya: That aligns with typical POCs. We'll propose specific checkpoints - we can include 32k and 64k context variants where available.
05:12 Jesse: Security questions?
05:15 Liam: SOC 2 in scope, audit logs, KMS integration for keys, and RBAC for teams. Also desire for SSO/SAML.
05:24 Maya: Redwood supports SOC2, KMS/HSM integrations, SSO/SAML, and detailed audit logs. For Private we can support customer-managed KMS and stricter network controls. We'll attach the security whitepaper.
05:38 Aisha: Data residency? Some parts of our product need EU-only hosting.
05:42 Jesse: We have regions in EU and NA; for Private you can control deployment region. We'll note that in the follow-up.
05:52 Sofia: What about embeddings? We use them for reranking - can we host embedding models close to the generator to reduce cross-region latency?
05:59 Maya: Yes, you can colocate. For lowest latency we recommend running embeddings and generator in same cluster/region, or even same Dedicated pool.
06:10 Liam: How do you handle model fallbacks? If the high-quality model is busy, can we fallback to a cheaper variant automatically?
06:17 Jesse: Yes - smart routing policies can route by latency, cost, and SLOs; automatic fallback to compatible variants is supported. We'll show config examples in the POC plan.
06:31 Aisha: Any showstoppers we should be aware of? For instance, licensing for certain open weights.
06:36 Maya: We'll call out license constraints in the model catalog; some weights have academic or noncommercial clauses - we avoid those for production. For Dedicated/Private you can bring-your-own-weights in some cases if licenses allow.
06:50 Liam: For the POC dataset, we will provide 500 long threads (avg length 8k tokens) and a reranking test set.
06:58 Jesse: Perfect, that will help us measure end-to-end latency and cost per successful resolution.
07:05 Sofia: Timeline question - we want a pilot in January and decision by end of Jan. Is that feasible?
07:10 Jesse: Yes - POC kickoff early January, run 2 weeks of benchmarking and a short evaluation.
07:18 Maya: On the technical side we'll need sample data, access patterns, and success criteria - F1 for slot extraction, CTR lift for rerank, and median latency.
07:30 Liam: We'll define success metrics and share them with Maya.
07:36 Aisha: Anything else on tool-calling? We might need secrets passed to internal APIs. Does Redwood support per-call secrets or vault integration?
07:44 Maya: We support integrations with KMS and secrets managers; for Private you can bring your KMS. For Hosted and Dedicated we offer managed KMS with tenant isolation.
07:55 Jesse: We'll include integration notes in the security doc.
08:00 Jesse: Alright, quick recap - POC with two model variants (high-quality and optimized multilingual), run on Dedicated, evaluate EN/ES/FR, measure cost/latency/quality, and check tool-calling and security integrations. Next I will send pricing and the bench spreadsheet. Maya will draft POC plan. Customer to send data and metrics.
08:20 Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks all.
08:24 Jesse: Thanks - we'll follow up with the items discussed. Happy holidays.

Transcript notes: occasional filler and overlaps, some model names transcribed as "Mixtral" or "Mistral fork" - see attached model catalog link listed in follow-up.
